mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5%, it indicates a strong labor market which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE falls below 5% but SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) and employment growth (PAYEMS) jointly indicate a strong economy, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If both GDPC1 and PAYEMS show growth but SPX returns are negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, if FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it may lead to higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% but SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates economic expansion and increased consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO exceeds 105 but SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is below 1% and UNRATE is above 5%, it indicates a unique monetary policy stance that may lead to increased liquidity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but SPX returns are negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During an economic expansion, growth in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS grows but SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis fails.
